Rule Content: WAIT UP TO' should be avoided and used only where it is explicitly required for queue management scenarios.
NO Nested SQL statements must be used
No, EXIT or CHECK statements be used between SELECT and ENDSELECT.
Negative conditions not to be used  because they disabled usage of the index
Field symbols always be checked for assignment before use and explicitly unassigned with UNASSIGN when no longer needed, as using CLEAR can be unsafe (see rule SECU-010 for shared memory).

Use aggregation functions (MIN, MAX, COUNT, etc.) with GROUP BY instead of SELECT / ENDSELECT. This lets the database do the calculation efficiently and improves performance significantly (up to 700%).

If only some fields are required, select only those fields instead of all columns.
This improves performance and reduces memory usage.
SELECT SINGLE must be used only when the full primary key is specified; otherwise, SELECT UP TO 1 ROWS must be used, even though SELECT SINGLE is approximately 10% more efficient.

Rule: JOIN vs FOR ALL ENTRIES vs nested SELECT
Rule Content: Join (or view) are more efficient than nested select ( between 200 and 300%). As redundant data can appear in the result (in case of 1:N cardinality) a restrictive list of field MUST be specified in the selected fields ( ie : you MUST NOT use SELECT * FROM …)
On SAP HANA (SoH/S4), result set ordering is not guaranteed; therefore, every SELECT statement must explicitly specify an ORDER BY clause.
FOR ALL ENTRIES has poor performance characteristics and should be avoided in favor of JOIN or RANGE-based selections.
Whenever possible, SORTED or HASHED internal tables should be used, or appropriate DEFAULT/SECONDARY keys should be defined to ensure optimal performance.
For BINARY SEARCH, the internal table must be sorted according to the fields specified in the search condition
Use SELECT * in database queries. Always retrieve only the required fields to minimize database load, memory consumption, and network traffic.
Use ORDER BY in SELECT statements whenever the sequence of retrieved records is relevant to program logic or subsequent processing.
Use appropriate primary or secondary key fields in the WHERE clause to avoid full table scans and improve database performance.
Use INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF for large-volume data retrieval. Prefer direct mapping into appropriately typed internal tables (TABLE OF).
Perform direct SELECT statements on pooled or cluster tables. Use SAP standard Function Modules, APIs, or provided access methods.
Prefer database JOINs over FOR ALL ENTRIES. When FOR ALL ENTRIES is required, use suitable RANGES and packet processing while considering SAP limitations for high-volume selections.
Perform repeated database access to the same table within loops, such as executing SELECT statements inside LOOP, DO, or WHILE constructs.
Use SY-SUBRC to validate the result of database operations. Do not rely on SY-DBCNT, IS INITIAL, or IS ASSIGNED immediately after a database SELECT.
Perform initial and validation checks before executing any UPDATE, MODIFY, or DELETE operation on database tables to prevent unintended data changes.
Check SY-SUBRC after database operations (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MODIFY), READ TABLE, file interface operations (OPEN DATASET, READ DATASET), ASSIGN, and CALL FUNCTION statements.
Sort internal tables before performing multiple reads and use BINARY SEARCH where applicable to improve lookup performance.
Use nested loops on large datasets. Prefer techniques such as Parallel Cursor, Hashed Tables, or Sorted Tables for efficient processing.
Use Standard Tables when frequent insertions, deletions, or modifications of key fields are expected.
Use Sorted Tables when the primary access pattern involves frequent reads using sorted or key-based access.
Use Hashed Tables when unique key-based access is required, particularly for master data, configuration data, or lookup-intensive scenarios.
Design, develop, and test programs considering expected production data volumes, input volumes, and output volumes to ensure acceptable runtime performance.
